title: Lesson 51 - The Feedback Wasn't Very Clear

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thanks for reviewing it. Could you be more specific about what feels cold in the opening?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: The heading says “Greeter Instructions,” and the first line begins with a rule. It doesn't explain why the role matters.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What would “warmer” look like in practice?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Keep the instructions, but start with one welcome line: “Thanks for helping visitors find the side gallery confidently.”

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That's clear. Can you give me an example of what feels impractical in the middle?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: The break handoff is a paragraph. A volunteer scanning a phone may not see the sequence quickly.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Are you suggesting that I turn it into numbered steps?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Yes—who contacts the backup, where the handoff happens and when the first person can leave.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So the change you're asking for is a three-step handoff, not more information.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Your third note says the contacts feel busy. Is the issue the number of contacts or the layout?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: The layout. The names, roles and extensions are all in one sentence.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Would a small table with the columns “Situation,” “Contact role” and “Extension” solve it?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Yes. Keep the three roles, but separate them visually.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Let me summarize the feedback to make sure I've got it right. You suggested adding one purpose line, asked me to turn the handoff paragraph into three numbered steps, and recommended a three-row contact table.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Correct. I also pointed out that none of those changes adds new scope.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Good. That's specific enough to act on. I'll revise those three locations and leave the approved content unchanged.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: When can I see the new version?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: By two tomorrow. Lena can check the wording at three, and Sam can verify the access and contact details before final sign-off.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: That works. Please show the changes in comments so we can verify that each note was addressed.
